sourceText.he: גְּמָ׳ וְאַמַּאי? יָבֹא עָלָיו כֹּהֵן מִשְּׁנֵי צְדָדִין, וְלֵימָא לֵיהּ: אִי בְּכוֹר הוּא – כּוּלֵּיהּ דִּידִי הוּא, וְאִי לָאו בְּכוֹר הוּא – הַב לִי מַתְּנָתַאי.
אָמַר רַב אוֹשַׁעְיָא: בְּבָא לִידֵי כֹּהֵן וּמְכָרוֹ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל בְּמוּמוֹ.

positions.claim: no slaughterer should be exempt, since the priest's claim succeeds on either horn of the doubt
positions.basis: reasoning from the structure of the doubt itself

positions.claim: the mishna speaks of a firstborn that already reached a priest and was sold by him to an Israelite once blemished, so the priest cannot claim the animal itself and the two-sided claim collapses
